entries.text: Decided on a wide wheel base and built the base robot — the chassis every attachment will mount to.
Decided: the drive wheels will use the 49.5 × 20 mm tires.
Started the Flip the Rock (M03) attachment — not finished yet.
Built the Lucky Leaves (M04) attachment.
Built the Drone Survey (M01) attachment.
Wrote the first version of the program template for the robot base — every mission program will start from it.
Kept building the robot base.
Created the Mission 12 (Forest Elder) attachment.
Worked on combining the Mission 2 and Mission 3 attachments into one — Exploding Seeds + Flip the Rock in a single run.
Worked on the Mission 2 (Exploding Seeds) attachment.
Updated every teammate's profile card in the app — the first real team data in it!
Finished the design of the robot base and built THREE copies of it — every attachment now has a base to test on.

Base decisions: low + wide (low center of gravity, more accurate turns; tradeoff = harder in tight spaces). Reinforced the base to make it rigid. Discussed color sensors — decided to use no sensors because the compact base had no room for one.
Finished the attachment for the Forest Elder (M12) and did the programming for it.
Did the programming for Drone Survey (M01) — our first mission program!
Made the team mascot AND an attachment for "the mascot mission" (M13 Keystone Species) — the robot will carry our mascot onto the restoration platform.
Programmed mission 4 (Lucky Leaves) — second mission program for Adeline.
Programmed the Forest Elder (M12).
Built the attachment for number 14 (Seeds of Renewal) — first attachment after finishing the robot base.
Built the attachment for number 2 (Exploding Seeds) and worked on number 8 (Tangled).
Built an attachment for mission 15 (Biocentric Architecture) — the 40-point mission!
Finished the Keystone Species (M13) attachment — the one that carries our mascot.
Programmed mission 14 (Seeds of Renewal) — the attachment Weston built.
Built and programmed the attachment for mission 15 (Biocentric Architecture).
Programmed mission 12 (Forest Elder).

Our solution idea: a camera to put in the forest. It has an AI camera to tag animals, solar panels and batteries so it can charge in the sun, and it sends the images to a website we built. Now gathering materials.
Fynn programmed mission 14 (Seeds of Renewal) and got 5/5 in the tests. Our first test session!
Adeline finished programming mission 15 (Biocentric Architecture) and mission 12 (Forest Elder).
Nolan programmed missions 2 and 3 (Exploding Seeds + Flip the Rock) and got 5/5 in his tests.
Weston worked on building the attachments for the tree mission.

Picked Option B: build the forest camera on our own Raspberry Pi 4, running 24/7 on solar. We already have the Raspberry Pi 4, an m5cam module, and a microSD card. Next: buy a camera, motion sensor, night light, solar panel, battery, and a waterproof box.

Coach CJ helped research a cheaper, low-power camera (Seeed XIAO ESP32S3 Sense) instead of the Raspberry Pi 4. It sleeps between animals and needs a much smaller solar panel, but it needs night vision added, and the animal tagging would happen later on a bigger computer. Deciding between XIAO only, Pi 4 only, or both together.

We will use the Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense board for the forest camera. It has Wi-Fi built in. Our Raspberry Pi 4 will connect to it over Wi-Fi to get the pictures. Next: test how far the Wi-Fi reaches in the forest.

Our coach helped us plan two cameras. Camera 1 plugs into power behind our house with a view of the forest, for testing and live streaming over Wi-Fi. Camera 2 goes in the forest in solar mode and turns on and off with movement. A switch picks "always on mode" or "solar mode": to collect pictures we walk up, flip it to always on so the Wi-Fi connects, download, then switch back. Both use USB-C power. Parts list made.

We met our first expert, Nate Reagan from Arizona Game and Fish. There are about 300 animal strikes in a year on I-17, and the I-17 wildlife bridge is supposed to reduce collisions by 90%. Baby animals follow their mom across. He said not to live stream, to use AI to blur out people, and that cameras over a wide area work best. We need ADOT's permission to use the bridge; if that doesn't work out, we could watch the squirrel nest.

We brought 5 questions for Nate Reagan (Game and Fish): how many animal crashes happen in Flagstaff, our blinking warning light idea, live stream cameras, how long animals take to trust a new bridge, and how they will count animals on the new I-17 overpass at Willard Springs. New idea: the camera makes a blinking light to warn drivers about an animal crossing (Nate said it has been done before).

We bought the parts for our camera. Solar box: 6V 3W solar panel, Waveshare Solar Power Manager (D), two 2600 mAh 18650 batteries (still shipping). Camera box: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense, AM312 motion sensors, DS3231 clock modules. The solar box and the camera box are two different options: the camera gets USB-C power from a phone charger, or from the solar box if there is no power nearby. We are starting by wiring the camera box while the batteries are delayed.

Nolan rebuilt the attachment for mission 13 (Keystone Species).
Weston built an attachment for mission 11 (Window to the Past), our first one for that mission.
Fynn programmed mission 4 (Lucky Leaves) and mission 5 (Reaching Roots). Isla helped Fynn.
Thea worked on the team app.
Nolan did the wiring for the camera. Thea helped Nolan.
Isla programmed the mascot mission (mission 13, Keystone Species).
Weston built an attachment and programmed the big tree mission (mission 9, Research Platform), our first one for that mission.

experts.name: Nate Reagan
experts.feedback: Don't live stream: that prevents bad stuff. Use AI to edit the video or blur out any people. Cameras over a wide area work best. Get our own data, and ask ADOT before using the I-17 wildlife bridge.
experts.improvement: Still deciding: live stream or not, the wildlife bridge or the squirrel nest (backup), one camera or several.
experts.notes: ["About 300 animal strikes in a year on I-17","The I-17 wildlife bridge cost $24 million and is supposed to reduce collisions by 90%","Baby animals go where their mom goes, so if the mom uses the bridge, they will too","GPS collars on elk: they tranquilize them to put collars on; the battery lasts 3 years, then the collar falls off","Game and Fish has a live stream to watch the animals","There might be one camera on the bridge (he is not sure)","A camera with a flashing light has been done before","Officers use satellite cameras that send a notification to your phone","Not using a live stream prevents bad stuff from happening","We could use AI to edit the video or blur out any human","We won't get data from Game and Fish, so we get our own","We need ADOT's permission to use the bridge","Backup: put the camera on the squirrel nest and track that","Cameras in a wide perimeter would be the most effective","Thermal goggles to see animals at night","Not a lot of AI; drones for law-enforcement investigations"]

tradeoffs.question: Low and wide, or tall and narrow?
tradeoffs.options: Low + wide base vs taller, narrower base
tradeoffs.why: Low center of gravity so it doesn't tip. Wide wheelbase makes turns more accurate. Tradeoff we accepted: harder to move in tight spaces on the field.

tradeoffs.question: Reinforce the base or keep it light?
tradeoffs.why: Made the base more rigid so it doesn't flex or twist — attachments line up the same way every run.

tradeoffs.question: Color sensors, or no sensors?
tradeoffs.options: Color sensors (line / color detection) vs none
tradeoffs.why: The base is so compact there was no room left for a sensor. Tradeoff we accepted: no line or color detection — the robot navigates by wheel rotations and turns alone.

tradeoffs.question: One robot base, or three identical copies?
tradeoffs.options: One base everyone shares vs three matching bases
tradeoffs.why: (students: write why here — more attachments tested at once? a spare if one breaks?)

tradeoffs.question: One attachment for Missions 2 + 3, or two separate ones?
tradeoffs.options: Adeline's Mission 2 attachment vs Nolan's combined 2 + 3 attachment
tradeoffs.why: Test both, then pick — and write down why. That's exactly what judges want to see.
